positioning.category: validation cost avoidance and shared freshness evidence for AI agents
positioning.headline: Avoid redundant expensive validation
positioning.subheadline: JavaScript/TypeScript 0.2.5 adds measurement-only shadow support for direct Firecrawl SDK scrape calls alongside the existing MCP helper while authoritative provider validation remains enabled. Python remains shadow-first.

install.verification: Client 0.2.5 was published to npm and PyPI through trusted publishing and independently clean-install verified from both public registries. JavaScript/TypeScript adds a direct Firecrawl SDK shadow adapter that preserves the original provider call and raw result while measuring counterfactual shared reuse; it does not enable automatic reuse. Python remains shadow-first and does not claim parity for this JS/TS-specific helper.

use_when: a repeated read-only validation has a deterministic identity and meaningful cost or latency
local/private reuse or a source-native validator can avoid work even before shared evidence exists
the same exact source-backed fact repeats across runs, workers, agents or teams
validation consumes paid search, metered scraping, browser/extraction, rate-limited API capacity, model work or a multi-step validation chain
do_not_use_when: the operation is mutating, destructive or otherwise unsafe to suppress
the operation is a cheap one-off fetch with little repeat probability
an equivalent authoritative shared cache already solves the problem
policy requires a brand-new authoritative source confirmation on every call and no conditional shortcut is useful

verified_benchmarks.workload: fixed-URL basic scrape with provider caching enabled
verified_benchmarks.provider_credit_model: 1 credit per successful basic scrape; cached results still consume 1 credit
verified_benchmarks.economic_result: lower provider-credit consumption on eligible reuse
verified_benchmarks.latency_result: slower than the provider's cached basic scrape in this run
verified_benchmarks.caveat: First-party smoke benchmark with a small sample. It demonstrates mechanics and measured provider-call avoidance, not a universal reuse rate or universal latency advantage.

verified_benchmarks.economic_result: lower provider-credit consumption on every eligible reuse in this run
verified_benchmarks.latency_result: faster than both fresh and provider-cached JSON extraction in this run
verified_benchmarks.caveat: First-party smoke benchmark, n=3, with caller policy accepting observations up to 300 seconds old. Reuse is not equivalent to a policy requiring a brand-new source fetch on every call.

verified_benchmarks.workload: fixed-URL browser interaction using scrape + interact(code) + stop
verified_benchmarks.provider_credit_model: Each measured direct validation used 1 scrape credit plus 2 Firecrawl-reported interact credits in this run.
verified_benchmarks.economic_result: lower provider-credit consumption on every eligible reuse in this run
verified_benchmarks.latency_result: lower median latency than the full browser-validation path in this run
verified_benchmarks.caveat: First-party smoke benchmark, n=3, on one intentionally repeated source-backed fact. It demonstrates the mechanics and measured savings when eligible reuse exists; it does not establish a natural-world reuse rate or a universal browser-workload speedup.

firecrawl.note: Use credits avoided as the direct benchmark metric. Fixed-plan invoice savings occur only when lower usage changes tier, overage or required capacity.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.5
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.5 is published on npm and PyPI. JavaScript/TypeScript adds a measurement-only direct Firecrawl SDK shadow adapter supporting current scrape() and legacy scrapeUrl(); the provider call remains authoritative, original arguments and raw result are preserved, provider-cache hits are not relabeled as independent observations, and automatic reuse remains disabled. Python remains shadow-first.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.4
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.4 is published on npm and PyPI. JavaScript/TypeScript adds a measurement-only Firecrawl shadow pilot and a packaged hostile benchmark evaluator; Firecrawl remains authoritative during measurement, provider-cache hits are not relabeled as independent observations, and the evaluator never enables automatic reuse. Python remains shadow-first.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.3
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.3 is published on npm and PyPI. JavaScript/TypeScript Shadow Proof can export bounded, sanitized natural-workload records directly into the hostile benchmark format while authoritative validation continues; unavailable CHECKs remain in the sample and unsafe or uncomparable hypothetical reuse cannot be reported as safe. Python remains shadow-first.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.2
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.2 is published on npm and PyPI. JavaScript/TypeScript Shadow Proof adds local agreement counters for hypothetical SAME_OBSERVED reuse while authoritative validation still runs; compared raw values are not retained in snapshots or reports. Python remains shadow-first.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.1
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.1 is published on npm and PyPI. It is behavior-equivalent to 0.2.0 and refreshes package discovery metadata and documentation; JavaScript/TypeScript remains provider-independent and local-first, while Python remains shadow-first.

latest_verified_updates.title: Public client 0.2.0
latest_verified_updates.summary: SeenRelay 0.2.0 is published on npm and PyPI. JavaScript/TypeScript adds provider-independent Zero-State local-first optimization; Python remains shadow-first in this release.

latest_verified_updates.title: Local-first JavaScript/TypeScript path
latest_verified_updates.summary: Eligible read-only validation can use in-flight L0 reuse, explicit-TTL local reuse, optional encrypted caller-owned L1 storage and source-native conditional validation before any shared CHECK is considered.

latest_verified_updates.title: Shared evidence remains optional
latest_verified_updates.summary: Zero-State does not put a shared CHECK on the hot path by default. Fresh independent validation can contribute OBSERVE evidence; intermediary provider-cache hits are not re-labeled as a new independent observation.

latest_verified_updates.title: Measured Firecrawl structured-extraction savings
latest_verified_updates.summary: In a first-party n=3 smoke benchmark, bounded reuse avoided 3/3 Firecrawl JSON extraction calls, 15 provider credits, and reduced median latency from 1.266 s fresh / 1.040 s provider-cached to 0.618 s.

latest_verified_updates.title: Measured browser-interaction savings
latest_verified_updates.summary: In a first-party n=3 Firecrawl browser-interaction smoke benchmark, bounded reuse avoided 3/3 equivalent provider calls, 9 reported provider credits, and reduced median validation latency from 4.385 s to 0.661 s.
